title: SharePoint and OneDrive agents: OneDrive files as knowledge sources
summary: Hold: Microsoft documents a preview Graph automation route for agent User access, which the briefing reports as undocumented. The low cost rating also conflicts with the documented pay-as-you-go meter; the roadmap facts and the printed control paths and commands are supported.

claims.claim: Disabling Microsoft Copilot for SharePoint per user blocks SharePoint agents and also disables Copilot in OneDrive and SharePoint page authoring Copilot.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Agent and plugin User access is configured at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Settings > User access.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Settings > User access to manage your organization's agents and plugins.

claims.claim: No automation is documented for tenant-wide agent and plugin User access.
claims.quote: These resources also support remediation and applyOnce. ... useraccess resource type ... userAssignmentCategory ... Specifies whether all users or no users can access agents and plugins. ... everyone, noOne
claims.fix: Replace controls[2].api with kind graph, call 'POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors', docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/configurationmanagement-post-configurationmonitors?view=graph-rest-beta'. Append to the note: 'Preview automation applies a baseline once with mode=applyOnce and resourceType=microsoft.agent.useraccess, resourceVersion=1; properties.valueObject.userAssignmentCategory sets everyone or noOne. This route does not document specific-user/group selection. Requires delegated ConfigurationMonitoring.ReadWrite.All for the caller, CopilotPolicySettings.ReadWrite for the TCM service principal, and an AI Administrator signed-in user.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/utcm-agent-resources. The operation reference states that applyOnce applies a desired-state baseline once.

claims.claim: All users is the default User access option.
claims.quote: All users - This option is the default. It means that all users in the organization can access agents and plugins, subject to the existing app policies and user assignments.

claims.claim: Answers follow each user's permissions to the source files, excluding content that the user cannot access.
claims.quote: the agent's responses depend on each user's permissions to the agent's data sources. ... if a user has access to the agent but not to the site or document library it references, the agent's responses for this user don't include content from those restricted sources.

claims.claim: Sharing access to the agent does not by itself grant access to its underlying OneDrive or SharePoint content.
claims.quote: Access to an agent doesn't grant access to its underlying SharePoint or OneDrive content. Users must have permission to both the agent and the knowledge sources it uses.

claims.claim: SharePoint agents require no activation and become available to licensed or pay-as-you-go-covered users on eligible sites where they have permissions.
claims.quote: Agents in SharePoint don't require activation. Once a user is assigned a Copilot license, or if your organization uses pay-as-you-go billing, these agents automatically become available to the user on eligible sites where they have permissions.

claims.claim: The low cost rating fits a briefing that documents metered unlicensed use.
claims.quote: cost: "low"; 'unlicensed use of SharePoint agents is billed ... under the Copilot Studio meter.' The standard defines low as indirect cost only and variable as metered.
claims.fix: Set cost to 'variable'. Replace the cost rationale with: 'Variable. Interactive use by authenticated Microsoft Copilot users is included at no extra cost, while unlicensed .agent-file use is metered at 12 messages per interaction under the Copilot Studio meter.' This is supported by https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/sharepoint-agents-azure-billing.

claims.claim: The restricted access control instruction has a corresponding controls-table row.
claims.quote: 'Apply restricted access control to the OneDrive accounts of people who hold restricted content'; the table has licence, service-plan, User access, block, Restricted Content Discovery and missing-source-switch rows, but no restricted access control row.
claims.fix: Remove the 'Apply restricted access control' checklist bullet; the controls table does not document this control. Keep the sourced explanatory mention in Risk assessment. Do not add a row as part of this correction.

claims.claim: The instruction to create a Purview DLP policy has a corresponding controls-table row.
claims.quote: 'Create a Purview DLP policy with a Sensitivity labels condition'; none of the six controls rows documents Purview DLP.
claims.fix: Remove the 'Create a Purview DLP policy' checklist bullet; no table row documents this control. Keep the sourced descriptive DLP statement in Risk assessment. Do not add a row as part of this correction.

claims.claim: The instruction to monitor usage through Management Shell, Purview audit and SharePoint Advanced Management has corresponding table controls.
claims.quote: 'Monitor agent usage with the SharePoint Online Management Shell, the Microsoft Purview audit log and SharePoint Advanced Management'; the table contains no usage-report or audit control.
claims.fix: Remove the monitoring checklist bullet because its monitoring controls have no rows. Do not add rows as part of this correction.
